chapters.title: Launch plan: blog, webinar, case study
chapters.gist: Leah lays out the Routing v3 GA launch (blog on Nov 17, webinar Nov 19, beta customer case study); Asher cautions the 11% miles number is only two weeks old and suggests locking it at the end of October and using the case-study fleet's own number.

chapters.title: Live ETA in the launch messaging
chapters.gist: Tom pushes to mention live ETA at launch because prospects keep asking; Asher firmly refuses to announce anything not scheduled and tells Tom to bring the deal impact to Q4 planning instead; Leah will write a no-date FAQ answer.

chapters.title: Pricing page update
chapters.gist: Routing v3 and the ML ETA model ship on all tiers with no price change at GA; Leah will drop the beta tag and add the miles claim with a footnote once the number is locked, and the RouteWise comparison page is pushed to December.

chapters.title: Timeline, owners and reference customers
chapters.gist: Leah owns the launch timeline (case study draft Oct 23, number locked Oct 30, customer approval Nov 6) and asks Tom for two beta reference customers; Tom will ask the Columbus parcel fleet and, via Sofia, Brightside.

turns.t: Hey. Hi. Okay, Tom's here. Asher, you're, I think you're on mute.
Am I? No, I'm here, sorry, I was finishing a Slack thread. Hi.
Hey hey.

Okay. So this should be quick-ish. I want to walk through the launch plan for Routing v3 GA, get you both to poke holes in it, and then I need a couple of things from Tom, which I'll get to at the end. So. GA is November seventeenth, that's a Tuesday. The plan is three pieces. One, a blog post that goes live the morning of the seventeenth, plus the customer email and the in-app banner, the usual stuff. Two, a webinar on the nineteenth, the Thursday, so two days later, where we basically walk through what changed and show a before and after on a real route. And three, a customer case study from one of the beta fleets. And that's the one I'm honestly most worried about, timeline-wise.
Why the case study specifically?

Because it needs a customer. Like, I can write the blog myself, I can run the webinar, but the case study needs a fleet to agree to be named, give us a quote, and then their legal or their comms person has to approve it. And in my experience that's three weeks minimum, sometimes six. And the whole thing kind of hinges on the number. The eleven percent. Fewer miles driven. That's the headline. If we have an actual fleet manager saying, you know, we're driving eleven percent fewer miles, that does more than anything I could ever write.
That number's real, right? Like we're not going to get burned on it later.

It's real, but it's early. Beta started September eighth, so we have, what, two weeks of data. Eleven percent fewer miles, and on-time went from ninety-one point two to ninety-four point six. I'd expect it to roughly hold, but I don't want to promise it's exactly eleven in November. It could be ten, could be twelve.
Okay, that's useful. So when do you want me to lock the number?

Give me until the end of October. By then it's like seven, eight weeks of data across all six fleets, and Daniel can pull the final number properly. And for the case study, honestly, the per-fleet number is better anyway, because it's their number, not our average.
Oh, that's a good point. So the quote would be their own, like, our fleet saw whatever percent.
Right. And it might be higher or lower than eleven for that fleet, and that's fine. We just say this fleet saw X, and the blog says the beta average was eleven.

Okay. And for the blog itself, I want to lead with the driver, not the algorithm. Like, nobody outside this building cares that it's a new solver. They care that their drivers get home earlier and their customers stop calling to ask where the van is. So the structure I have is the problem, what we built, the beta results, and then a section on the ETA model, because the ETA part is honestly what people will feel day to day.

Yeah, agree, lead with outcomes. I'd also say somewhere that it's the same product, same workflows, it's just smarter underneath. Because the number one question from existing customers is going to be, do I have to retrain my dispatchers.
Ooh, good. Do they?
No. That's kind of the point. Nothing really moves in the UI except the ETA confidence thing on the route panel.

Can we turn it into dollars, though? Because nobody on a buying committee cares about miles, they care about fuel and overtime. Like for a hundred-and-eighty-van fleet, eleven percent fewer miles is, I don't know, that's got to be a few hundred grand a year.

Careful. It depends completely on their miles per van and fuel cost. I did the napkin math for one of the beta fleets and it was more like, I think it was ninety k a year. Ninety-something. Which is great, but it's not a few hundred.
Okay, ninety k is still a great number.

It is, but I don't want a dollar figure in the blog that we made up for them. What I could do is a little calculator on the launch page. Enter your fleet size, your average miles, your fuel cost, and it shows the savings at eleven percent. Then it's their math, not ours.
I like that a lot more. Just make it say based on beta results, not a guarantee.

Yeah. Okay. So blog uses the aggregate, case study uses the fleet's number, calculator does the dollars. Webinar, I'm thinking forty-five minutes. Like fifteen of framing, twenty of a live demo, ideally Daniel or Kenji, and ten of Q and A. Asher, would you do the framing part with me?
Yeah, I can do that. Daniel for the demo, I'd say. Kenji's great but he'll go three layers deep into the model and lose half the room.

Okay, Daniel. I'll ask him. Not this week though, I know he's buried in the GA checklist. And for registrations, our last webinar got about a hundred and forty sign-ups and maybe sixty showed up live, so I'm aiming for three hundred registered this time. Which means invites have to go out at least two weeks before.
Can we do a second webinar slot for the West Coast? Last time we did one at nine Pacific and half my prospects were literally driving.
I mean, we could record it and send it out. I'd rather do one live and good than two live and meh.
Fine. Record it, send it, I'll chase people.
Okay, so while we're on messaging. I want to raise one thing. I really think live ETA needs to be in the launch somehow.
In what way?

Like, in the blog, in the webinar, something. Even just a coming soon. Prospects keep asking. Every single call. Harbor & Pine asked about it last week, Marcus literally called it a must-have. Brightside's asked twice. If we do this big launch that's all about ETAs and we say nothing about live ETA, it looks like we just don't have it, and RouteWise is already going around saying they have something.
No.
Asher.

No, sorry, I'll explain, but it's a no. Live ETA isn't committed. It's not on the Q4 roadmap yet, it's about five engineer-weeks, and it's competing with the driver app onboarding work for the same people. We haven't decided. And we are not going to announce something that isn't scheduled. That's just, that's a line for me.
It doesn't have to be a date. It can just be, like, we're working on it.

But we're not working on it. That's the thing. Priya's maybe sketching some stuff, but nobody's building it. And the minute it's in a blog post, every prospect, every customer, Brightside especially, they read that as a promise. And then if planning goes the other way, we've told three hundred fleets about something we're not doing. I'd rather lose a deal to RouteWise on a feature than lose a customer on trust.

I mean, I'd rather not lose the deal either. Harbor & Pine is three hundred ten k. That's not nothing. And they decide by October thirtieth, which is before we even launch. Their CFO is going to look at us next to RouteWise, and RouteWise is cheaper. Live ETA is one of the few things Marcus can point to and say, that's why we pay more.

I know exactly what it is. And honestly, if you want live ETA to happen, the way to make it happen is to bring it to Q4 planning. Bring me the deals, the dollars, which ones it's actually blocking. That's a real input. A blog post isn't.
Okay. Fine. I'll bring it. I still think we're leaving something on the table at launch.
Out of curiosity, what does RouteWise actually have? Because if they're claiming it, I want to know what we're up against in the messaging.
From what Marcus showed me, it's a shareable link with the driver on a map. It's, I mean, it's not great. I think it refreshes every fifteen minutes or something.
So it's not live.
It's not live. But it's a link a customer can click, and we don't have a link a customer can click.
Fair. That's a real gap, I'm not pretending it isn't. It's just not a launch message.

Can I suggest a middle ground that isn't really a middle ground? The launch is about better ETAs, period. Like, the model is way more accurate, six point one minutes of error down to four point three. That's real and it's shipping. And if someone asks in the webinar Q and A about live tracking, we just have an honest answer ready. Like, it's something we hear a lot, we don't have a date. That's it.
That I'm fine with. As long as the answer is literally we don't have a date.
And what do I say on calls?
Same thing. You can say it's one of the top things customers ask for and we're evaluating it for the roadmap. You cannot say Q4, you cannot say early next year, you cannot say soon.
Can I say soon-ish?
Tom.
I'm kidding. Mostly. Okay. I hear you.
I'll write up a little FAQ for the Q and A and for sales, so we're all using the same words. I'll send it to both of you this week.
Perfect, thank you.
Just put it on the record that I think this is a mistake.
Noted. It's literally being recorded.

Okay. Pricing page. So right now the pricing page says, under Pro and Enterprise, advanced route optimization, and there's a little beta tag next to ML ETAs, on Enterprise only. We need to update it for GA. Asher, what's the actual packaging? Is v3 everywhere or is it tiered?

v3 replaces the old solver for everyone, all tiers. We're not running two engines. The ML ETA model is the same, it's everywhere. What stays tiered is the stuff around it, so multi-depot and dispatcher overrides stay Pro and up, and the higher API limits are Enterprise. And prices don't change at GA.
Wait, so Starter gets the new engine too? Shouldn't that be an upsell?

We talked about that a lot. It's way more expensive for us operationally to run two engines than to just give Starter a better optimizer. And honestly a better Starter experience is how those accounts become Pro.
Okay. I'd have priced it differently, but fine.
Do we need to do anything for existing Starter customers? Like an email saying, hey, you're getting this for free?
Yeah, actually, that's a nice touch. It's a reason to talk to them that isn't a renewal. Fold it into the customer email, maybe a separate version for Starter.
That I like. Free stuff, I can sell.

So for the page: remove the beta tag, move ML ETAs up into the shared feature list at the top, and rewrite the optimization line. Can I put a number on the pricing page? Like, up to eleven percent fewer miles?

I'd avoid up to, it's kind of a sketchy phrasing. I'd do, beta fleets drove eleven percent fewer miles on average, with a footnote on what the beta was. And only once we've locked the number at the end of October.
Fine. Footnote. Legal's going to want that anyway. And the screenshots on that page are from the old dispatcher view, are those changing at GA?
Not much, the UI is mostly the same. The route detail panel has the new ETA confidence thing, so I'd reshoot that one. Ask Priya, she'll know which states look good.
Also, the comparison table. Can we take another look at the RouteWise comparison while we're in there? Because they're cheaper, and our table makes us look expensive without ever saying why.
That's a bigger project. I don't want to touch the comparison page in the same release, it's a separate page and it's a whole thing with legal. Can we do that in December?
December's fine, as long as it actually happens.
I'll put it on the list. With your name next to it so you can yell at me.

Okay, last bit. Timeline and owners. I'll own the overall launch timeline, I'll put it in the doc today with every date. Roughly: case study interview mid-October, draft by the twenty-third, customer approval by November sixth. Blog draft by October thirtieth, Asher reviews it. Lock the miles number October thirtieth too. Webinar invites go out November second. Pricing page changes staged by November tenth and flipped on the seventeenth with everything else. Does that sound sane?

Sounds sane. Leave buffer on the customer approval though, that's always the thing that slips. And wait, you said invites November second, but you also said two weeks before for three hundred registrations. That's only seventeen days.
Oh. Yeah, okay, that's tight. Let me pull invites up to the twenty-seventh of October. I can do the registration page without the final number.
And the demo route, Asher, I want it to be a real one. Can we use an actual beta route, anonymized?

Should be fine with the customer's okay. Daniel has this replay tool that shows the old route and the v3 route side by side, it's really nice actually, you can see the van stop zigzagging across the same neighborhood.
Oh, that's the money shot. I want that in the blog too, like a little looping GIF.
Ask Daniel. After the checklist, please.
And for the blog, can Maya do a technical accuracy pass after me? I don't want to say something about the solver that makes Daniel wince.

Yes, good, I'll add her as a reviewer. Okay, so Tom, here's my ask. I need two beta customers who'd be willing to be references. One for the case study, named, with a quote. And a second one as a backup, or for the webinar, ideally someone who'd come on live for five minutes and say nice things. Who do you have?

Hmm. So of the six beta fleets, the Columbus parcel fleet is probably the happiest. Their ops guy is very chatty, he'd love to be on a webinar. Brightside, maybe. Jordan likes us, but they're the ones asking about live ETA every other week, so putting them in front of an audience...
Yeah, I'd be careful with Brightside on a live webinar. The Q and A could get spicy.

Right. For the case study though, Brightside's actually kind of perfect. It's grocery, it's three metros, it's a name people recognize. And their renewal's in January, so making them the hero of a story isn't the worst thing for us either.
Ooh, I like that. Can you ask them? And the Columbus folks?
I'll ask both this week. I'll talk to Sofia first on Brightside, since she owns the relationship. I don't want to just show up out of nowhere asking for favors.

Great, yes. And when you ask, mention we'll need them to sign off on the miles number for their fleet, so it's not a surprise later. And if neither says yes, we can do an anonymized one, like a regional grocery fleet, but honestly those are worth about half as much.
Got it. They'll say yes. And I'll bring the live ETA deal list to planning.
Please do. With numbers.
Okay, I think that's it. I'll send notes and the timeline. Thanks, both.
Thanks, Leah. This is a good plan.
Thanks. Still mad.
Bye, Tom.

general.tldr: Routing v3 GA launches Nov 17 with a blog post, a Nov 19 webinar and a beta-customer case study; Asher firmly kept live ETA out of launch messaging because it isn't scheduled, and Tom will line up two reference customers.

items.text: Review Leah's launch plan for Routing v3 GA (Nov 17) and get two reference customers from Tom.
Three launch pieces: blog post plus customer email and in-app banner on Nov 17, a 45-minute webinar on Nov 19, and a named case study from a beta fleet.
The 11% fewer-miles result is only two weeks old; Asher wants it locked at the end of October, and the case study should use the featured fleet's own number.
Live ETA stays out of all launch messaging. It is not committed (about 5 engineer-weeks, competing with driver onboarding), and Asher won't announce what isn't scheduled.
Routing v3 and the ML ETA model ship on every tier including Starter, with no price change at GA.
Blog leads with outcomes for drivers and dispatchers, not the solver, and reassures customers there's no retraining since the UI barely changes.
Instead of quoting a dollar figure (Tom guessed a few hundred thousand; Asher's napkin math for one fleet was ~$90k/yr), Leah will build a savings calculator on the launch page.
Webinar: Leah and Asher frame, Daniel demos (not Kenji, who would go too deep), aiming for 300 registrations vs. 140 last time; one live session, recorded for the West Coast.
Demo will use a real anonymized beta route with Daniel's side-by-side replay tool, which Leah also wants as a GIF in the blog.
Tom wanted at least a coming-soon because prospects keep asking: Harbor & Pine calls it a must-have and Brightside has asked twice.
Asher: nobody is building it, a blog mention reads as a promise to 300 fleets, and he'd rather lose a deal on a feature than a customer on trust.
RouteWise's version is a shareable map link that refreshes about every 15 minutes, so it isn't live, but Asher acknowledged it's a real gap.
The approved answer for Q&A and sales calls is that it's a top customer request being evaluated, with no date. No Q4, no early next year, no soon.

Remove the beta tag, move ML ETAs into the shared feature list, and use the claim that beta fleets drove 11% fewer miles on average, with a footnote and only after the number is locked. Avoid 'up to'.
Existing Starter customers get a version of the launch email telling them they're getting v3 at no extra cost.
Tom's request to rework the RouteWise comparison table is deferred to December.
Leah publishes the full launch timeline in the launch doc today.
Tom asks the Columbus parcel fleet and Brightside (via Sofia) to be references this week.
Tom brings the list of deals blocked by live ETA, with numbers, to Q4 planning.

project_update.tldr: Launch plan for Nov 17 GA is set and owned by Leah. The main risks are case-study approval lead time and the 11% number moving before it's locked on Oct 30.

items.text: On track. Plan agreed: blog + email + banner on Nov 17, webinar Nov 19, case study approved by Nov 6, pricing page staged by Nov 10.
Beta results so far: 11% fewer miles and on-time delivery up from 91.2% to 94.6% after two weeks.
Messaging set: lead with outcomes, use the ML ETA improvement (6.1 to 4.3 min error) as the ETA story, with no live ETA mention.
Packaging confirmed: v3 is on every tier with no price changes at GA.
Case-study customer approval typically takes 3–6 weeks; Asher asked for buffer because it always slips.
The 11% figure is based on two weeks of data and could land at 10–12%, so nothing ships with the number until it's locked.
Webinar invites originally planned for Nov 2 left only 17 days to reach 300 registrations; moved to Oct 27.
Brightside is a risky live webinar guest given their repeated live ETA asks.
Sales disagrees with leaving live ETA out of launch while Harbor & Pine ($310k, deciding Oct 30) compares Tandem with the cheaper RouteWise.
Lock the miles number with Daniel by Oct 30.
Leah writes the live ETA FAQ for webinar Q&A and sales this week.
Maya does a technical accuracy pass on the blog after Asher.
Tom secures two reference customers.

highlights.title: Lock the 11% number late October and use the fleet's own figure
Asher: we won't announce live ETA because it isn't scheduled
Brightside for the case study, Columbus fleet for the webinar

ask.q: Why isn't live ETA part of the Routing v3 launch?
ask.a: Asher said no because live ETA isn't committed. It's about 5 engineer-weeks, it competes with driver onboarding for Q4 capacity, and nobody is building it. Announcing it would read as a promise to ~300 fleets. He told Tom to bring the affected deals to Q4 planning instead.

ask.q: What is the launch plan and timeline?
ask.a: Blog post, customer email and in-app banner on Nov 17, a webinar on Nov 19, and a beta-customer case study. Case-study draft by Oct 23 and customer approval by Nov 6. Blog draft and the locked miles number by Oct 30. Webinar invites move up to Oct 27. Pricing page changes are staged by Nov 10. Leah owns the timeline.

ask.q: Can marketing use the 11% fewer-miles number?
ask.a: Yes, but not yet. It comes from only two weeks of beta data and could end up at 10–12%, so Asher wants it locked at the end of October. The blog and pricing page will say beta fleets drove 11% fewer miles on average, with a footnote and no 'up to'. The case study will use the featured fleet's own number.

ask.q: Which customers might be references for the launch?
ask.a: The Columbus parcel fleet is the happiest beta fleet and a good live webinar guest. Brightside is a strong case-study candidate (grocery, 3 metros, renewal in January) but risky on a live webinar because of their live ETA asks. Tom will ask both this week and go through Sofia for Brightside.

ask.q: What changes on the pricing page?
ask.a: v3 and the ML ETA model ship on every tier with no price change. The beta tag comes off, ML ETAs move into the shared feature list, and a footnoted 11% miles claim is added once the number is locked. Reworking the RouteWise comparison table is deferred to December.
